title: Normalized Roos descent of fixed strict stalk towers
statement: Fix ell different from D.p, a coherent integral comparison system I, and already fixed strict data T satisfying [lem-trf-strict-stalk-towers]. There exists full data S extending exactly T, satisfying TrfStalkTowerDescentLaws and TrfStalkCompositorQuotientCompatible. The descent laws assert the strict-cone factor equations for comparison and reparametrization, the canonical two-coordinate section factor equation, integralNormalized, derived reparametrization and identity, and sectionsComposition for the specified entire-system compositor. They do not assert integralCompositor, integralIteration or integralPointUnit: those are derived in the parent by categorical algebra.

source.place: Tag 0F4F (lemma-point-functor): the combined-colimit identification behind the finite composition germ formula; agent extension to the entire-tower counit realization, original Steps 3, 6, 7; blueprint thm-trf-l-function-euler-product.proof.md, Step 1, Local powers, input (b).

proof.text: Exact finite stalks and coefficient restriction preserve levelwise quasi-isomorphisms; exact module products preserve them on both coordinates of the Roos cone. Thus stalk Roos realization inverts system quasi-isomorphisms.

Localize the strict maps c and r and their diagonal cone maps. The localization comparison gives factors, comparisonFactors and reparamFactors; uniqueness descends the strict reparametrization and identity squares.

Exact point sections preserve the products in the normalized Roos bridge. Compose the bridge, the canonical scalarRoosMap and the cone map of e to obtain sections and sectionsFactors. The strict finiteSections equation gives sectionsComposition after descent.
Define integral as point sections of the specified pullback realization followed by sections. This proves integralNormalized by construction.

For every simultaneous K-flat presentation, take finite stalks of kappa to construct the strict tower isomorphism z. Its germ formula, finiteUnit and sectionGerm identify the composite with every normalized eP. Substitute the pullback-model normalization and the section factor equation; functoriality of the diagonal cone gives precisely quotient compatibility. The common bounded truncation zigzag identifies this arrow without imposing bounded K-flat terms.
Naturality for chain maps, inversion for quasi-isomorphisms and composition for roofs extend the equations to all derived arrows and representatives.

lean.statement:
theorem trfStalkTowerDescent (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (I : IntegralComparisonSystem.{u} l)
    (hI : IntegralComparisonRealizationCoherence l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) I)
    (T : TrfStrictStalkTowerData l E D) (hT : TrfStrictStalkTowerCoherent l E D T) :
    ∃ S : TrfStalkCompositorTowerData l E D I,
      S.toStrict l E = T ∧ TrfStalkTowerDescentLaws l E D I S ∧
        TrfStalkCompositorQuotientCompatible l E D I S
